newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Damaged German freighter still stuck off Iceland.
newsitem.headline: Damaged German freighter still stuck off Iceland.

text.p: A German container ship which ran aground off the Icelandic coast two days ago was still stuck on Friday and salvage looked unlikely, an Icelandic coast guard official said.

The 8,000 tonne vessel, the Vikartindur, went aground at 1947 GMT on Wednesday about 1.5 nautical miles from the Icelandic coast after being struck by a heavy wave. It had been drifting for about two hours because of engine trouble.
The official said the ship was still listing 40 degrees on its starboard side towards the sea. Insurance companies and the ship's owners were at the site.
"There is very little possibility of salvaging the vessel. There is a large crack in it," said the official, who asked not to be named, by telephone from Reykjavik.
One Icelandic coast guard worker was lost after falling overboard in an attempt to tow the vessel when it went aground on Wednesday. The body has not been recovered.
All 19 of the German crew were safe after being rescued from the ship by helicopter.
A small amount of the 350 tonnes of bunker oil onboard the ship had begun to leak, but the expected oil pollution had still not occurred, the official said.
No one could board the ship because of the bad weather, below freezing temperatures with snow and gales measuring around 50 knots.
The ship was leased by Iceland's largest shipping company, Eimskip, and owned by German shipping company Peter Dohle Schiffahrts Kg.
It was carrying containerised cargo from Germany to Iceland, the official said.
